background_sources_outside_window.title: MRI enhancement foundation model

background_sources_outside_window.design_impact: Head-to-head of classical ML, 2D/3D CNN, transfer learning and 3D ViT on the same paired MRI/PET data. Best balanced accuracy 0.815 came from a hybrid that included hippocampal volume, i.e. an explicit volumetric feature, not from the largest architecture. Supports the plan's refusal to assume scaling buys accuracy.
background_sources_outside_window.note: URL 10.3389/fnins.2024.1387196 is a 2024 publication. Previously listed as 2025 in the registry; moved to background rather than used as window padding.
background_sources_outside_window.title: Comparison of deep learning architectures for predicting amyloid positivity from T1-weighted brain structural MRI

sources.design_impact: Directly instantiates d1: BrainIAC is a 3D brain-MRI SSL foundation model (SimCLR-contrastive ViT-B) producing global latent embeddings, pretrained on 32,015 of 48,965 multiparametric scans and evaluated on seven tasks with the largest gains in low-data regimes (e.g., IDH AUC 0.79 vs 0.61-0.68 for Scratch/MedicalNet/BrainSegFounder at 100% data; MCI AUC 0.88; tumor Dice 0.79). It supplies the BrainIAC-style backbone and benchmark protocol (linear probing, few-shot K=1/K=5, 10-100% data fractions) that the CAFT d1 arm adopts. It does not implement d2 (baselines are MedicalNet/BrainSegFounder/Scratch at 96^3 inputs, not a locked local 128^3 CNN on identical subject-level splits), d3 (no amyloid/PET endpoint), d4 (scanner variability only simulated as synthetic contrast/Gibbs/bias perturbations, no real scanner/site confound probe), or d5 (no calibration, abstention, or conformal sets). True external test sets exist only for brain age and survival, so cross-scanner generalization of the embeddings themselves is untested in this source.
sources.title: A generalizable foundation model for analysis of human brain MRI

sources.design_impact: Core overlap is d3: a transfer-learning chain from brain age to cognition to amyloid predicts PET-defined amyloid status from MRI plus demographics (sex, age, APOE genotype) without PET input, with SUVR RMSE 0.175 in both ADNI(test) and CANDI and amyloid positivity AUC 0.742 (ADNI test) and 0.796 (CANDI), rising to 0.905 and 0.803 in dementia subgroups (CN-vs-dementia cognition AUC approx 0.95). It evidences both the feasibility and the modest accuracy ceiling of MRI-only amyloid inference in a multi-cohort setting with a fully held-out cohort. It is a supervised 3D-CNN-plus-transformer model (not an SSL foundation embedding), so it does not instantiate d1 or the locked 128^3 local CNN on identical subject-level splits of d2. No scanner/site confound probe (d4) beyond post-hoc attribution of CANDI degradation, and no abstention or conformal prediction (d5).
sources.title: Deep-learning based multi-modal models for brain age, cognition and amyloid pathology prediction

sources.code_weights: pretrained models publicly released at https://github.com/EIDOSLAB/AnatCL
sources.cohort: 7,908 individuals / 21,155 T1w images from public datasets: pretraining on OpenBHB healthy controls (3,984 multi-site scans aggregated from ABIDE 1/2, CoRR, GSP, IXI, Localizer, MPI-Leipzig, NAR, NPC, RBP); downstream ADNI (all phases; 633 HC, 712 MCI, 409 AD; 14,385 images), OASIS-3 (685 patients, 88 AD; 1,354 images), SchizConnect (383), ABIDE-I (1,102)
sources.confound_audit: not_reported (multi-site pretraining corpus acknowledged, but no explicit scanner/site/cohort confound representation probe)
sources.design_impact: This source overlaps CAFT dimension d1 as a CNN-based brain-MRI foundation-model embedding: a 3D ResNet-18 pretrained with an anatomy-aware weakly contrastive loss (age + cortical thickness/gray-matter volume/surface area similarities over Desikan-Killiany or Destrieux ROIs) and read out by linear probing. Its concrete numbers — brain age MAE 2.55 vs 2.66 (y-Aware) and 2.70 (ExpW), OASIS-3 AD detection up to 78.3 vs 74.7 balanced accuracy, but ADNI HC-vs-AD 80.8 not beating ExpW 81.8 and sMCI-vs-pMCI 65.9 below the age-supervised L1 baseline 68.1 — bound what a modest 3D CNN encoder with anatomical weak supervision achieves, directly informative when positioning a locked local 128^3 CNN comparator (d2) against BrainIAC-style global embeddings (d1). It has no PET-defined endpoints (d3), no site/scanner confound probing (d4), and no uncertainty-aware abstention (d5).
sources.endpoint: AnatCL weakly contrastive foundation model (3D ResNet-18) pretrained on healthy controls, evaluated by frozen-encoder linear probing on 12 deep-phenotyping tasks (brain age MAE 2.55±0.07 years and sex balanced accuracy ~80% on OpenBHB; schizophrenia broad/strict, schizoaffective, bipolar on SchizConnect; autism/Aspergers/PDD-NOS on ABIDE-I; HC-vs-AD on ADNI 79.4–80.8 and sMCI-vs-pMCI 64.8–65.9 balanced accuracy; HC-vs-AD on OASIS-3 74.3–78.3) plus 10 clinical assessment score predictions (AIMS, depression, handedness, GAIT, FIQ/VIQ/PIQ)
sources.external_validation: transfer evaluated on four datasets not used for pretraining proper (ADNI, OASIS-3, SchizConnect, ABIDE-I) under linear probing, but no held-out site/cohort stratification and no pretraining–downstream overlap audit reported
sources.modality: T1-weighted structural brain MRI (VBM-preprocessed modulated gray-matter maps) plus tabulated FreeSurfer anatomical measures used as weak supervision, not as input
sources.preprocessing: standardized VBM pipeline with CAT12: non-linear registration to MNI template, gray-matter extraction, 1.5 mm isotropic output at 121x145x121, modulated GM images via the brainprep package; anatomical features (cortical thickness, gray-matter volume, surface area) computed with FreeSurfer 6.0.5.1 using Desikan-Killiany (68 ROIs) and Destrieux (148 ROIs) atlases
sources.split: pretraining on OpenBHB healthy-only scans; downstream transfer via frozen encoder + per-task linear classifiers evaluated with 5-fold cross-validation, mean and SD across folds; downstream datasets distinct from the pretraining set, although OpenBHB itself aggregates ABIDE-1 healthy controls while ABIDE-I is used downstream (overlap not explicitly audited)
sources.title: Anatomical foundation models for brain MRIs
sources.uncertainty: mean and standard deviation across five cross-validation folds reported for all tasks; no confidence-interval significance testing between methods, no calibration, abstention, or conformal analysis

sources.design_impact: Overlaps d1 as a CNN-based alternative to BrainIAC-style global-embedding foundation models: a high-resolution SimCLR ResNet-18 pretrained on 44,958 T1w scans whose fine-tuned version beats supervised ResNet-18/ViT-T and MAE on all four tasks (Alzheimer AUC 0.929 vs 0.869; age MAE 4.35 vs 4.85 years; stroke MAE 5.37 vs 5.47) and still outperforms supervised baselines trained on all data when fine-tuned with only 20 percent of labels. Its protocol of comparing a pretrained encoder against supervised-from-scratch CNNs on identical splits informs the CAFT d1-vs-baseline comparison style, but the encoder is a ResNet-18 on 150x192x192 crops, not the locked local 128^3 CNN of d2. It has no amyloid/PET endpoint (d3), no scanner/site confound probe (d4), and no calibrated abstention or conformal prediction (d5).
sources.title: Building a General SimCLR Self-Supervised Foundation Model Across Neurological Diseases to Advance 3D Brain MRI Diagnoses

sources.design_impact: Provides the strongest clinical-transfer evidence relevant to d1: 19 foundation models benchmarked on clinical tasks under few-shot finetuning and cross-country domain shift (India/USA finetune to Denmark test), where 16 of 19 pretrained models outranked the supervised out-of-domain baseline and the best models beat even in-domain supervised baselines (ashash +10.51 AUROC over Supervised-ID on infarct classification; FOMO2JOMO -2.09 Mean AE on brain age). Its findings that local MAE-style objectives favor segmentation while hybrid reconstruction-contrastive objectives favor classification, and that small models were competitive with no reliable benefit from scaling size or pretraining duration, directly constrain design choices for the CAFT d1 embedding and d2 CNN arms. Site/vendor shift is the evaluation axis (partial d4 relevance) but no explicit scanner/site embedding-confound probe is run, and there is no amyloid/PET endpoint (d3) and no calibrated abstention or conformal prediction (d5). Inference-only container evaluation also confounds pretraining quality with finetuning recipes, a limitation the authors themselves state.
sources.title: Towards Brain MRI Foundation Models for the Clinic: Findings from the FOMO25 Challenge

sources.design_impact: Directly instantiates d4 with a travelling-heads scanner/vendor confound probe of frozen global embeddings, covering the d1-relevant BrainIAC and 3D-Neuro-SimCLR: BrainIAC shows poor between-scanner ICC 0.45 despite good within-scanner ICC 0.81 (23.1 percent scanner variance, 33.3 percent fingerprint), 3D-Neuro-SimCLR ICC 0.25 (32.0 percent scanner, 89.1 percent fingerprint) and BrainSegFounder ICC 0.31 (57.9 percent scanner), versus biology-guided AnatCL 0.97, y-Aware 0.81, and FreeSurfer 0.93, with pretraining strategy rather than architecture, dimensionality, or scale the strongest correlate. It supplies CAFT both the audit methodology (ICC(2,1)/ICC(3,1), variance decomposition, fingerprinting, subject identification) and a direct caution that pure-SSL global embeddings carry roughly 23-58 percent scanner-attributable variance, threatening any d1-vs-d2 comparison that does not balance or probe site effects. It does not address d3 (no amyloid/PET endpoint) or d5 (no abstention or conformal prediction), and only partially touches d2 (CNN versus Transformer embeddings are compared, but there is no locked 128^3 CNN arm). The authors note preprocessing is entangled with model choice, so reliability differences cannot be fully attributed to the pretraining objective alone.
sources.title: Cross-Scanner Reliability of Brain MRI Foundation Model Embeddings: A Travelling-Heads Study

sources.design_impact: This preprint tests whether MRI-to-amyloid PET synthesis is intrinsically ill-posed because amyloid and neurodegeneration are temporally decoupled. With 3D pix2pix, the Baseline model trained on all A/N regimes reaches only 57.4 percent balanced accuracy (corr 0.16) on the full test set, while Concordant-only and Discordant-only training reach 82.3 and 83.2 percent in-distribution; adding plasma biomarkers via FiLM lifts the plasma-subset test (n=199) from 64.5 to 85.3 percent balanced accuracy and correlation from 0.21 to 0.75. It overlaps CAFT d3 (PET-free inference for PET-defined amyloid status) and d5 (it demonstrates a one-to-many MRI-to-amyloid mapping that directly motivates ambiguity-aware calibrated abstention rather than architectural complexity), and its A/N-stratified evaluation informs biological-confound audits adjacent to d4. It uses no foundation-model embeddings and no locked CNN comparator (no d1/d2).
sources.title: When Brains Disagree: Biological Ambiguity Underlies the Challenge of Amyloid PET Synthesis from Structural MRI

sources.design_impact: This preprint distills a BiomedCLIP-ViT teacher trained with Centiloid-aware triplet mining on paired PET-MRI into an MRI-only student, reaching best AUC 0.74 on OASIS-3 (T1w+T2w distilled to T1w) and 0.68 on ADNI, versus 0.61 for the T1w MRI-only baseline of Kim et al. (+19.7 percent), with cross-dataset distillation ADNI-to-OASIS-3 at AUC 0.72-0.73. It overlaps CAFT d3 directly (PET-free inference for PET-defined amyloid status with CL greater than 20.6 labels and no clinical covariates at inference) and is adjacent to d1 (frozen pretrained ViT encoder with LoRA, but a 2D general biomedical image-text model rather than a 3D brain-MRI foundation embedding). It reports no locked local CNN comparator on identical splits, no cohort/scanner confound representation probe, and no calibrated abstention (no d2, d4, d5).
sources.title: Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation for PET-Free Amyloid-Beta Detection from MRI

sources.design_impact: This preprint presents BrainDINO, a DINOv3-style slice-wise 2D ViT-B/16 brain-MRI foundation model pretrained on 6.6M unlabeled axial slices from 20 datasets, evaluated with a frozen encoder and lightweight heads across six task families at 10-100 percent label ratios. On ADNI under strict subject-disjoint splits, frozen BrainDINO reaches macro-AUC 0.850 for CN-vs-AD and 0.701 for CN-vs-MCI at full supervision versus BrainIAC at 0.725 and 0.588, and brain-age MAE 5.54 years versus BM-MAE 9.12 and BrainIAC 19.40; frozen adaptation matches or beats full fine-tuning on the harder classification tasks. It overlaps CAFT d1 directly (a brain-MRI foundation-model global embedding benchmarked head-to-head against BrainIAC under frozen probing, including low-label regimes) and its perturbation and sequence-classification analyses partially inform d4 (acquisition-shift robustness). It contains no amyloid/PET endpoint (no d3), no locked local CNN trained on identical subject-level splits (no d2), and no abstention or conformal analysis (no d5).
sources.title: Frozen Brain MRI Foundation Model Representations Generalize Across Clinical Tasks

sources.design_impact: This short preprint decomposes frozen foundation-model predictions into anatomical region contributions: FastSurfer-defined regions are encoded separately by frozen BrainIAC or NeuroFM and combined by a region-additive logistic head in which every region contributes an explicit scalar term. RegionFM matches fine-tuning on OASIS-1 cognitive impairment classification (BrainIAC 0.751 plus-minus 0.083 versus 0.759 plus-minus 0.089 ROC-AUC; NeuroFM 0.717 plus-minus 0.082 versus 0.645 plus-minus 0.088), and randomized embedding ablations fall to near chance (0.475-0.505). It overlaps CAFT d1 (frozen BrainIAC global embeddings under an interpretable additive head) and its region-additive attribution could localize d1/d2 predictions at region level. It has no amyloid/PET endpoint (no d3), no cohort/scanner confound probe (no d4), and no uncertainty calibration or abstention (no d5).
sources.title: RegionFM: Interpretable Region-Based Brain MRI Classification Using Foundation Model Embeddings

sources.design_impact: This preprint benchmarks two generalist foundation models (BrainIAC, 3DINO) and two segmentation foundation models (MedSAM2, Medical-SAM2) against from-scratch CNN baselines on African versus non-African brain MRI. BrainIAC linear probing reaches ROC-AUC 0.85 plus-minus 0.06 on the Nigerian dataset versus 0.80 plus-minus 0.05 on OASIS-4 (LoRA 0.86 plus-minus 0.05 and 0.81 plus-minus 0.02), while zero-shot MedSAM2 attains 0.86 plus-minus 0.01 Dice on BraTS-Africa versus 0.82 on EGD-150; gaps (up to 0.09 ROC-AUC and 0.13 Dice) are inconsistent in direction and the larger EGD training set lifts all models to 0.80-0.82 Dice, attributing differences mainly to dataset size rather than origin. It overlaps CAFT d4 directly (explicit cohort/population confound evaluation of foundation-model embeddings, including age-confound caveats and size-matched controls) and d1 partially (BrainIAC global embedding under linear probing and LoRA). The from-scratch DenseNet121 baseline shares the identical MCCV splits but is not a locked local 3D 128-cube CNN (only partial d2 spirit); there is no amyloid/PET endpoint (no d3) and no calibrated abstention (no d5).
sources.title: Do Medical Foundation Models Generalize on the African Brain?

sources.design_impact: ADLIP is a vision-language model for AD/MCI/CN, not PET-defined amyloid. It uses 3D T1 MRI plus structured clinical text (MMSE, APOE, CSF Abeta/tau, FAQ). HABS-HD zero-shot accuracy was 0.64 (95% CI 0.60-0.67). Outside Method X and not the five-component CAFT combination.
sources.title: A vision-language foundation model for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis using MRI and clinical data

sources.design_impact: MCI-to-AD conversion, not PET-defined amyloid. Single-timepoint ResNet3D c-index about 0.70; longitudinal CNN+LSTM 0.80-0.90; time-window AUC > 0.85. Relevant to a future R2 survival branch, not to the current CAFT residual gate.
sources.title: Longitudinal structural MRI-based deep learning and radiomics features for predicting Alzheimer's disease progression

sources.design_impact: 3D CNN AD vs CN accuracy stayed stable after intensity binarization; models used skull-strip contours (Clever Hans). Direct justification for the R1a mask-edge gate before trusting BrainIAC embeddings.
sources.title: Skull-stripping induces shortcut learning in MRI-based Alzheimer's disease classification

sources.code_weights: not_reported (data sharing statement deferred to Supplement 3; no code or model release described in the full text)
sources.cohort: 2,916 cognitively unimpaired participants (final sample after excluding one extreme outlier; mean age 66.9 [9.9] years, 57.2% women, 38.1% APOE e4 carriers, 33.3% Aβ-positive; 1,747 with both Aβ PET and CSF) from 12 independent cohorts in the US, Europe, Australia, and Canada (ADC n=46, ADNI n=241, AIBL n=180, ALFA n=359, BioFINDER-1 n=105, BioFINDER-2 n=595, Knight ADRC n=383, MCSA n=363, PREVENT-AD n=217, SPIN n=171, TRIAD n=103, WRAP n=153), data June 2009–March 2024
sources.confound_audit: cohort heterogeneity handled by within-cohort z-scoring anchored on Aβ-negative >50-year-olds, Centiloid PET standardization, and cohort-specific CSF thresholds; PPV/NPV reported by age strata (PPV 38% under 60 years rising to 93% at 80+, NPV falling 91% to 66%); acknowledged limitation: Aβ prevalence slightly higher than the general cognitively unimpaired population and need for validation in more diverse samples
sources.design_impact: This peer-reviewed JAMA Neurology study is the key fluid-biomarker comparator for CAFT dimension d3 — PET-free inference of PET-defined amyloid status in exactly the cognitively unimpaired, preclinical-AD population CAFT targets — quantifying the current ceiling: AUC 83%, stand-alone PPV 79% at 95% specificity capturing only 46% of Aβ-positive cases, and 2-step confirmation reaching 91-99% PPV while cutting PET/CSF testing by over 40%. Its prevalence-aware PPV/NPV analysis and age-stratified degradation supply the decision-theoretic benchmark any MRI-based PET-free amyloid classifier must meet or exceed, and its 2-step triage logic is a non-imaging analogue of d5-style deferred/abstained decisions, though implemented purely with operating-point thresholds rather than calibrated abstention or conformal sets. It contains no brain-MRI modeling, so it does not overlap d1, d2, or d4.
sources.endpoint: accuracy of plasma p-tau217 (immunoassay, with age as covariate) for classifying amyloid-beta status defined by CSF or Aβ PET in cognitively unimpaired adults: stand-alone AUC 83% (95% CI 81-85); at 95% specificity threshold PPV 79% (74-84), accuracy 81% (80-82), detection of only 46% of Aβ-positive cases; at 97.5% specificity PPV 85% (80-90) with sensitivity 35%; 2-step workflows (plasma-positive confirmed by PET or CSF) raise PPV to 91% (86-95) vs PET reference and 99% (98-100) vs CSF reference; trial-recruitment simulation: screening 677 people with plasma vs 536 with PET-alone to enroll 100 Aβ-positive individuals while reducing PET tests to 124-139; mass spectrometry vs immunoassay head-to-head (n=964): accuracy 88% vs 82% (P<.001), Aβ+ detection 69% vs 49% (P<.001), PPV 85% vs 80% (P=.12)
sources.external_validation: not a train/external-test design: 12 independent international cohorts pooled with within-cohort z-harmonization; generalization probed via assay-stratified, cohort-stratified (BioFINDER-2-only), age-stratified, and alternative-cutoff sensitivity analyses rather than a held-out cohort
sources.modality: plasma p-tau217 (primary immunoassays: Lilly MSD and Janssen Simoa; mass spectrometry comparison subset n=964) with age covariate; reference standard Aβ status from CSF (Aβ42/40 or p-tau181/Aβ42, cohort-specific thresholds) or Aβ PET (11C-PiB, 18F-flutemetamol, 18F-florbetapir, 18F-NAV4694; Centiloid >25 or visual read); no MRI input
sources.preprocessing: plasma p-tau217 log10-transformed and z-scored within each cohort based on Aβ-negative participants older than 50 years, excluding extreme outliers (<Q1-5IQR or >Q3+5IQR) for cross-cohort harmonization; PET standardized to the Centiloid scale with positivity >25 CL (sensitivity thresholds >12 and >37); cohort-specific CSF positivity thresholds as previously validated
sources.split: positivity thresholds derived by cutpointr on 30% of the sample (optimizing sensitivity at 95% or 97.5% specificity) and locked, then evaluated on the remaining 70%; logistic regression with age covariate; mass-spectrometry comparison thresholds computed on the full n=964 subset due to smaller sample; single-assay single-site sensitivity analysis (Eli Lilly at Lund, n=1670)
sources.title: Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 to Identify Preclinical Alzheimer Disease
sources.uncertainty: bootstrap with 1000 resamples for variability of PPV/NPV/accuracy with 95% CIs throughout; extensive threshold sensitivity analyses (specificity 75–97.5%, Centiloid 12/25/37, covariates none/age/age+APOE e4, cost ratios 1:4:16 to 1:8:20); no calibration curves, conformal prediction, or abstention framework (the 2-step confirmatory workflow plays the practical role of uncertainty management)

sources.design_impact: ShareGAN synthesizes 3D amyloid PET from structural MRI (SSIM about 0.90; PET+/- accuracy 88.5% and 89.4% on two external sets). PET is the training target, so this is synthesis rather than PET-free Method X inference and is not CAFT.
sources.title: MRI-to-PET synthesis via deep learning for amyloid-beta quantification in Alzheimer's disease

sources.design_impact: Uses amyloid-PET during pretraining (RCMD) and reports CN/AD and CN/MCI endpoints (relative +6.2% / +7.0% vs missing-modality baselines). Not Method X (PET enters training) and not the five-component CAFT residual gate.
sources.title: BrainAnytime: Anatomy-Aware Cross-Modal Pretraining for Brain Image Analysis with Arbitrary Modality Availability

sources.design_impact: Strongest available comparator: same endpoint, and it includes A4. 4056 development plus 149 external exams. T1-only AUC 0.61, T1+FLAIR 0.67 internal, 0.65 external, MCI subgroup 0.71. This is the realistic performance envelope for the Method X endpoint and it uses A4, so the CAFT gap claim must be stated against it, not against ADNI-only numbers. PubMed 40579043 is the same article; s02 was merged rather than double-counted.
retrieval_attempts_20260822: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=DOI:%2210.3174/ajnr.A8899%22&format=json (record found: AJNR Am J Neuroradiol 2025;46(12):2590-2598, PMID 40579043; isOpenAccess N, inPMC N, inEPMC N, no full-text URLs)
sources.title: Deep learning-based prediction of PET amyloid status using MRI: multicontrast EfficientNet with independent external validation

sources.design_impact: CSF Abeta cutoff 980 pg/ml; multimodal accuracy 0.762 +/- 0.04 with guided-backprop XAI. Requires sMRI+rs-fMRI+dMRI, so it is outside the T1-only Method X contract. Scope comparator only; does not implement CAFT.
sources.title: Multimodal MRI accurately identifies amyloid status in unbalanced cohorts in Alzheimer's disease continuum

sources.code_weights: uses only publicly available tools (ComBat, HACA3, HD-BET, LST-AI, FSL FAST, ANTs); no new code or model weights released by the authors
sources.cohort: ADNI3 (2016-2022) retrospective: scanner-group analysis of 1,143 subjects (233 GE, 173 Philips, 250 age-matched Siemens selected by KDE probabilistic sampling, plus 487 Siemens subjects as an independent harmonization reference group; one GE subject excluded for HACA3 processing failure with missing brain tissue post-harmonization); within-subject comparison of 8 subjects with paired multi-vendor scans within 3 years (4 GE/Siemens, 3 Philips/Siemens, 1 GE/Philips); mean ages 75.8-76.3 years in analysis groups
sources.confound_audit: directly a scanner-confound study: baseline vendor effects quantified for G/W ratio (T1w GE 0.73±0.02 vs Siemens 0.77±0.02; T2-FLAIR GE 0.98±0.05 vs Siemens 1.13±0.06) and logWMH; age-matched Siemens group constructed via KDE sampling; preservation of the age-WMH biology checked (r = 0.393 baseline, 0.381 ComBat, 0.412 HACA3 vs 0.496 Siemens-only reference); ComBat preserves age/sex/cognitive-status covariates; warns that both tools substantially shift absolute WMH volumes and can erase pathology (HACA3 reduced WMH contrast in individual cases)
sources.design_impact: This source overlaps CAFT dimension d4 most directly: it is an explicit, quantified scanner/vendor confound analysis on ADNI — the very dataset family CAFT-style amyloid-prediction work will train on — showing that baseline vendor batch effects (e.g., T2-FLAIR G/W ratio spanning 0.98-1.13 across vendors) are reduced but not eliminated by ComBat or HACA3, with HACA3 best on FID (10.45 to 5.60 T1w) yet capable of erasing WMH pathology. Its evidence that harmonization choice materially moves downstream image-derived measurements supplies concrete caution and ready-made metrics (FID, LPIPS, G/W ratio) for any confound-probe protocol (d4) attached to d1/d2 pipelines. It involves no PET-defined endpoints (d3) and no uncertainty-aware prediction (d5).
sources.endpoint: quantification of scanner-vendor differences in ADNI3 3T T1w and T2-FLAIR and comparison of two publicly available image-level harmonization methods — statistical ComBat vs deep-learning HACA3 — on gray/white-matter contrast ratio, log white-matter-hyperintensity volume (LST-AI segmentation), Frechet Inception Distance, and LPIPS; headline: mean FID T1w/T2-FLAIR improves 10.45/14.62 (baseline) to 7.45/11.71 (ComBat) to 5.60/8.91 (HACA3), and only HACA3 yields non-significant between-vendor WMH differences (ANOVA p = 0.083)
sources.external_validation: no cohort external to ADNI3; authors flag as a limitation that ADNI3-specific protocols may not generalize to other datasets, and vendor effects persist significantly post-harmonization in several metrics
sources.modality: 3T T1w and T2-FLAIR brain MRI under standardized ADNI protocols
sources.preprocessing: N4 bias-field correction; T2-FLAIR co-registered to T1w with ANTs; both spatially normalized to MNI152 1mm (antsApplyTransforms); harmonization arms: ComBat on flattened voxel-intensity arrays (batch = scanner vendor; biological covariates age, sex, cognitive status; Siemens target batch) and HACA3 deep-learning harmonization with anatomy disentanglement (inputs padded to 192x224x192, averaged Siemens reference template); skull-stripping with HD-BET and min-max intensity normalization to [0,1] in all arms
sources.split: retrospective group-comparison design rather than predictive train/test: evaluated vendor groups harmonized toward an independent Siemens reference group (n=487) disjoint from the 250-subject age-matched Siemens analysis group; Part 2 uses within-subject paired scans as their own controls
sources.title: Evaluation of Image-Level Harmonization Methods for Multi-Center MR Neuroimaging
sources.uncertainty: one-way ANOVA with Games-Howell post-hoc for vendor differences, repeated-measures ANOVA with Bonferroni-corrected paired t-tests for within-subject metrics, Steiger's Z-test for correlation comparisons, significance p<0.05; no predictive-uncertainty, calibration, or abstention methods (not a prediction study)

sources.design_impact: This source overlaps CAFT dimension d5 (ambiguity-aware calibrated abstention / conformal prediction sets) directly, and no other dimension: it is EEG spectrogram classification, not brain MRI. Its central quantitative lesson is that neighborhood conformal prediction (personalized calibration via k-NN relevance weighting) lifted random-split coverage on TUEV at alpha=0.2 from 0.53 (Naive CP) to 0.87 with only a modest set-size increase (1.22 vs 0.90), yet under patient-level splits every method (Naive, Covariate, K-means, NCP) fell well short of the 1-alpha target, with NCP's personalization yielding overly tight sets under strong shift. For CAFT this argues that conformal abstention must be validated under subject-level (not random) splits, exactly the regime where the i.i.d. calibration assumption breaks. The patient-distribution-shift framing is conceptually adjacent to d4 cohort confounds, but no confound representation probe is performed, and the suggested use of stronger foundation-model embeddings (TFM-Tokenizer) is left as future work.
sources.title: Making Conformal Predictors Robust in Healthcare Settings: a Case Study on EEG Classification

sources.design_impact: This source overlaps d3 (PET-free inference for amyloid status) most directly: predicting amyloid positive/negative from T1-MRI features, where all four generic SSL methods (SimCLR, Barlow Twins, Models Genesis, LSSL) underperformed FreeSurfer features (p<0.0001) and the auxiliary-informed R-NCE beat FS (p<0.0001). It also overlaps d1/d2 methodologically: frozen 3D brain-MRI SSL representations evaluated with linear heads on identical ADNI subject splits (2,431 patients) against a locked classical morphometric baseline (104 ComBat-harmonized FS features), with concrete numbers such as AD vs CN and AD vs MCI improved by R-NCE over FS (both p<0.0001) and 2-/3-year conversion improved (p<0.0001) while 5-year showed no significant difference. Its cautionary headline -- generic SSL lacks the biomarker sensitivity of hand-crafted features -- is a direct warning for BrainIAC-style embeddings unless domain-informed objectives are added. The pretrain-on-UKB+OASIS-3 / evaluate-on-external-ADNI design is a strong template for CAFT's external validation dimension; no conformal or calibration analysis so no d5 overlap, and cohort harmonization (ComBat) touches d4 only partially without an embedding-level confound probe.
sources.endpoint: biomarker_sensitivity_tasks_on_adni: binary_disease_classification (ad_vs_cn_mci_vs_cn_ad_vs_mci), ad_conversion_prediction_at_2_3_5_years, amyloid_status_classification (positive_vs_negative_used_as_proxy_for_more_expensive_markers), age_regression, plus_brain_age_gap_derived_measures (neuropathology_associations_and_gwas); metrics_auroc_and_r2_from_1000_bootstrap_samples
sources.title: A Cautionary Tale of Self-Supervised Learning for Imaging Biomarkers: Alzheimer's Disease Case Study

sources.design_impact: Most direct overlap with d1: BrainIAC's frozen 3D global embedding with a linear probe was benchmarked on identical patient splits against 2D encoders (MRI-CORE, BiomedCLIP, BrainDINO) and locked tabular baselines (radiomics + LogReg / TabPFN), and the MRI-specific encoders BrainIAC and MRI-CORE consistently ranked last or near-last within-cohort, with BrainIAC poorly calibrated (in-distribution ECE 0.15-0.32, external 0.30). It also informs d2 (locked linear-probe protocol on identical subject-level splits with a strong non-deep baseline: TabPFN reached 0.92 (0.03) AUROC / 0.74 (0.17) AUPRC versus 0.85 (0.08) for the best visual encoder BiomedCLIP) and d5 partially (ECE-based calibration audit showing ranking winners are not calibration winners, e.g. BiomedCLIP's external AUROC 0.74 (0.07) came with ECE 0.13 vs TabPFN 0.073). Cross-cohort and external post-treatment transfer (UCSD-PTGBM, drops of 0.10-0.30 AUROC) addresses d4-style site/prevalence shift empirically but without an explicit confound representation probe. No PET or amyloid task, so no d3 overlap.
sources.title: A Benchmark of (MRI-) Foundation Models to Predict IDH Mutational Status in Glioma

sources.design_impact: Overlaps d1 directly and d4 partially: it probes BrainIAC's own 3D brain-MRI foundation-model global embedding (768-d final class token) alongside four other 3D encoders (3DINO, BrainFM, NeuroVFM, Neuro-SimCLR) for sensitivity to acquisition artifacts on 95 multicenter BraTS-Africa cases (13,300 corrupted volumes; 7 artifacts x 5 levels x 4 modalities). BrainIAC was the most artifact-sensitive encoder, with linear CKA approaching zero under frequency-domain perturbations (k-space spikes, ghosting, Gibbs ringing), while 3DINO (100,000 multi-organ volumes) was the most consistently stable -- evidence that brain-specific pretraining and larger scale alone do not guarantee invariance to acquisition nuisance, a core concern for d4-style confound robustness of d1 embeddings. A key methodological finding is geometric drift without dimensional collapse (CKA drops substantially while RankMe stays nearly constant), and an independent TumorSynth segmentation reference aligned only partially (ghosting Dice declined 0.79 to 0.69 from L1 to L5). No clinical endpoint, no subject-level splits, and no calibration or abstention, so no direct d2, d3, or d5 overlap.
sources.title: Do 3D Medical Foundation Models See Through MRI Artifacts? A Controlled Study of Representation Robustness

sources.design_impact: Overlaps d1 (large-scale 3D brain-MRI SSL foundation model pretrained on FOMO60k, 60,529 scans) and provides conceptually important negative evidence for d3: modality-invariant contrastive learning (MCL) aligned cross-modality embeddings almost perfectly (mean cosine distance 0.0066 +/- 0.0104 vs 0.5995 +/- 0.1576 for default CL) yet did not improve lesion segmentation (ATLAS v2 DSC at 100percent training data: CL+MIM 0.4936 vs MCL+MIM 0.4782 vs CL 0.4678 vs MCL 0.4693 vs from-scratch 0.4188), because fine-grained modality-specific features proved essential -- each modality captures tissue characteristics not inferable from the others. This cautions that a globally aligned embedding may emphasize patient-level anatomy over modality-specific pathology signal, tempering expectations for cross-modality (e.g. PET-free) inference from a shared representation. There is partial d4 relevance via multi-center center-wise held-out test sets, though no explicit site/scanner confound probe, and no d2 or d5 overlap (segmentation endpoint, frozen-then-finetuned encoders, no calibration or abstention).
sources.title: Large-Scale Modality-Invariant Foundation Models for Brain MRI Analysis: Application to Lesion Segmentation

sources.cohort: pretraining on 20,000 heterogeneous brain MRI volumes sampled from 26 datasets of the FOMO300K superset; downstream: UCSF-PDGM (IDH, 495 cases), OASIS-1 (MCI, 235 samples), pooled HCP S1200/LONG579/SALD/Calgary/PETfrog/IXI (AGE, 3,578 samples, ages 2–39), BraTS GLI (1,251) + BraTS PED (99)
sources.confound_audit: exact pretraining–downstream file-path overlap audit reported per task with an overlap-removed MCI cross-level transfer re-analysis (gap closure 173.9% JEPA / 106.4% MAE after removal); no explicit cohort/scanner/site confound representation probe reported
sources.design_impact: This preprint directly overlaps CAFT dimension d1: it pretrains 3D ViT-Base MAE/JEPA encoders on 20,000 brain MRI volumes and benchmarks them head-to-head against BrainIAC and four other foundation models on identical folds (e.g., IDH linear AUROC 0.8767 ours vs 0.7486 BrainIAC; MCI 0.7533 vs 0.5289; BraTS GLI/PED macro Dice 0.8033 vs 0.6502). Its central result — P2 (orientation + resampling + foreground clipping + z-score) captures most utility, with best-level gains of only 3.4/1.8 pp and most paired gains statistically unresolved, while MCI's P7 gain is largely recoverable by downstream-only processing (68.6% JEPA / 81.1% MAE gap closure) — is a concrete precedent for treating preprocessing as a costed design variable in any d1 vs d2 comparison. It does not address PET-defined endpoints (d3), explicit site/scanner confound probes (d4), or calibrated abstention/conformal methods (d5).
sources.endpoint: preprocessing-level (P0–P7) cost–utility sweep for MAE/JEPA 3D ViT-Base brain-MRI foundation-model pretraining, evaluated by frozen-encoder transfer to IDH status prediction (best linear AUROC 0.8767, JEPA P6), MCI classification (0.7533, JEPA P7), brain-age regression (kNN MAE 2.4676 years, JEPA P5), and BraTS GLI/PED tumor segmentation (macro Dice 0.8033, JEPA P2), with kNN/linear/few-shot/fine-tune protocols
sources.external_validation: no fully external downstream cohort (authors explicitly defer this to future work); instead an exact file-path overlap audit between the 20k pretraining corpus and downstream sets (MCI 37/235 = 15.7%, AGE 312/3,578 = 8.7%, IDH 0/495, BraTS 0/1,350) plus an overlap-controlled MCI re-analysis; external pretrained encoders (BrainIAC, GenBrain, MedicalNet/Med3D, MRI-Core, RadFM) used as performance baselines rather than external data
sources.modality: multi-sequence structural brain MRI: T1w, T2w, FLAIR, T1c
sources.preprocessing: graded P0–P7 spectrum with measured cost per volume: P0 ROI crop native (1.92 s), P1 +RAS reorientation/resampling (3.40 s), P2 +foreground percentile clipping +z-score normalization (4.87 s, lowest feasible level; P0/P1 failed with NaN gradients and loss collapse before one epoch), P3 +N4 bias-field correction (60.07 s, 12.33x P2), P4 +brain extraction (31.94 s), P5 +affine template alignment (6.69 s), P6 +affine-initialized B-spline deformable alignment (178.54 s, 36.66x P2), P7 combined N4+brain extraction+affine (89.12 s, 18.30x P2); fixed 192^3 input, 16^3 non-overlapping patches, foreground-patch validity mask at 0.05
sources.split: fixed five-fold cross-validation for IDH/MCI/AGE (held-out fold test-only; validation ~10% of development pool, stratified by label and, for IDH, WHO grade; subject-grouped and age-bin/dataset stratified for AGE); BraTS dataset-specific 0.7/0.1/0.2 splits seed 42 (GLI 876/125/250, PED 69/10/20); identical folds across all evaluated models; downstream preprocessing matched to each model's own pretraining input definition
sources.title: How Much MRI Preprocessing Is Enough? A Cost–Utility Study for Brain MRI Foundation Models
sources.uncertainty: paired bootstrap 95% CIs and paired sign-flip tests with BH correction across 24 P2-vs-best comparisons — only 7/24 CIs excluded zero, only one nominally significant, only one survived BH; aggregate P2-to-best gap +3.4 pp (MAE) and +1.8 pp (JEPA); no calibration, abstention, or conformal analysis

sources.code_weights: public GitHub repository with Python scripts, model checkpoints, and study-population information (https://github.com/vkola-lab/ncomms2025); data available per-cohort on request; decision thresholds chosen by Youden's J on the validation split
sources.cohort: 12,185 participants from seven cohorts: training 10,352 (A4, NACC, OASIS3, AIBL, FHS), test 1,833 (external ADNI and HABS plus held-out NACC* with neuropathological data); 7,561 Abeta-negative / 4,624 Abeta-positive; 3,488 with tau PET (833 meta-temporal positive); postmortem validation in ADNI (n = 41) and NACC (n = 147)
sources.confound_audit: cohort-level confound handling present but not a representation probe: ComBat harmonization of tau SUVr across cohorts with pre/post ANCOVA cohort-effect testing, cross-cohort participant deduplication (OASIS/ADNI/NACC matching with exclusion of potential duplicates), and subgroup performance stratification; acknowledged limitations — predominantly White participants, no non-AD or mixed dementia cases, binary PET thresholds vary across studies
sources.design_impact: This peer-reviewed study is the strongest retrieved overlap with CAFT dimension d3: it performs PET-free inference for PET-defined amyloid (and tau) status at scale, reaching 0.79 AUROC (AP 0.78) for Abeta and 0.84 AUROC (AP 0.60) for meta-tau on external ADNI/HABS/NACC* test data, and quantifies prescreening utility via NPV/PPV trade-offs. It provides secondary d4 evidence (ComBat cohort harmonization with ANCOVA checks, cross-cohort deduplication, demographic subgroup analyses) and partial d5 motivation (probability-threshold triage to avoid unnecessary PET scans) but includes no calibration curves, confidence intervals, or abstention/conformal machinery. Notably, MRI additions raise meta-tau AUROC from 0.53 to 0.74 but the framework is tabular-plus-embeddings, not a 3D brain-MRI foundation-model global embedding, so it complements rather than implements d1/d2.
sources.endpoint: transformer-based multimodal prediction of PET-defined biomarker status from non-PET clinical data: global Abeta positivity (AUROC 0.79, AP 0.78), meta-temporal tau positivity (AUROC 0.84, AP 0.60), six regional tau labels (macro AUROC 0.80, AP 0.42; per-region AUROC 0.71–0.84), with alignment to centiloid (Pearson r = 0.58), meta-tau SUVr (r = 0.59), ADAS-Cog13, and postmortem Thal/Braak/CERAD/CAA grades, plus a PPV/NPV-based PET prescreening scenario (Abeta NPV 75.35%, PPV 62.05%; tau NPV 91.65%, PPV 52.40%)
sources.external_validation: yes — fully external test on ADNI (54% fewer features than NACC*) and HABS (72% fewer features) plus held-out NACC*; additional postmortem validation on ADNI (n = 41) and NACC (n = 147) neuropathology cohorts; subgroup AUROC/AP stratified by age, gender, race, education reported in supplement
sources.modality: 443 harmonized UDS3 clinical features (demographics, medical history, functional/neuropsychological scores, APOE e4, plasma Abeta42/40) plus MRI (FastSurfer T1w regional volumes; Swin UNETR embeddings of bias-field-corrected T1w, FLAIR, T2*w); amyloid and tau PET used only as labels, never as input
sources.preprocessing: T1w segmented with FastSurfer for regional volumes; Swin UNETR embeddings from bias-field-corrected volumetric T1 and FLAIR/T2* resampled to 1 mm and padded to 256^3 (embeddings 768x8x8x8); tau SUVr harmonized across cohorts with ComBat (batch = cohort; covariates age, sex, amyloid status, diagnosis) verified by ANCOVA with BH adjustment; Abeta positivity 24 CL (FHS DVR 1.20; NACC n=4,006 binary UDS variable); tau positivity from two-component GMM on harmonized training data (meta-ROI SUVr 1.37; regional thresholds 1.32/1.33/1.38/1.29/1.30/1.23)
sources.split: training 10,352 split into 8,281 train / 2,071 validation with stratified splitting across all labels; test 1,833 from ADNI, HABS, and NACC* never used in training; NACC train/test splits inherited unchanged from the original pretrained 13-label transformer protocol to prevent subject leakage; no cases excluded for missing data (random feature masking and label masking during training)
sources.title: AI-driven fusion of multimodal data for Alzheimer's disease biomarker assessment

sources.code_weights: training/fine-tuning/evaluation code public at https://github.com/Moona-Mazher/BrainFound (PyTorch, MRIPreprocessor); pretrained weights not_reported
sources.cohort: ~10,000 volumetric brain MRI scans (Table B1 total 10,663; 9,286 train/val, 1,377 test) from 12 public datasets: BraTS, ReMIND, UPENN-GBM, UCSF-PDGM, Burdenko-GBM-Progression, HABS, OASIS, ADNI, NACC (1,812), AIBL, NIFD, FeTA; subjects ~18–90 years
sources.confound_audit: not_reported (cross-dataset transfer used as a generalization check, but no explicit scanner/site/cohort confound representation probe)
sources.design_impact: This preprint overlaps CAFT dimension d1 as an alternative brain-MRI foundation-model recipe: DINOv2 ViT-Large with natural-image initialization plus brain-specific self-distillation, processed slice-wise rather than natively in 3D. Its headline results (AD AUROC 0.883 on NACC internally and up to 0.880 cross-cohort, MCI 0.766 on ADNI) and its demonstration that DINOv2-style self-distillation beats SimCLR/SwAV/MoCo-v3/MAE on these tasks give a concrete comparator family for a BrainIAC-style global embedding, while the authors themselves flag the loss of full volumetric context as a key limitation — directly relevant when contrasting d1 embeddings against a locked local 3D CNN (d2). It contains no PET-defined endpoints (d3), no site/scanner confound probing beyond cross-dataset transfer (d4), and no uncertainty-aware abstention (d5).
sources.endpoint: BrainFound (DINOv2 ViT-Large initialized from LVD-142M natural-image weights, further self-supervised on brain MRI) evaluated on disease detection (AD AUROC: NACC 0.883, ADNI 0.810, OASIS 0.857, AIBL 0.732; LBD 0.843; FTD 0.854; MCI 0.766; UCSF tumor grading 0.780), cross-dataset external AD transfer (NACC-trained to ADNI 0.830 / OASIS 0.880 / AIBL 0.799; ADNI-trained to NACC 0.765 / OASIS 0.706 / AIBL 0.732), few-shot learning at 10–100% label fractions, and segmentation (FeTA fetal tissues, BraTS 2020 tumor subregions; Dice and HD95)
sources.external_validation: yes — six cross-cohort AD evaluations training on one dataset (NACC or ADNI) and testing on independent cohorts, plus out-of-domain tasks (fetal FeTA, UCSF tumor grading) under protocols differing from training
sources.modality: brain MRI T1w, T2w, FLAIR (stacked channel-wise as RGB-like 3-channel input; single-modality scans duplicated across the three channels); no PET or fluid inputs
sources.preprocessing: standardised pipeline per Dorent et al.: co-registration of modalities in MNI space and skull-stripping; volumetric scans converted to stacked axial 2D slices (3 x 224 x 224) for the slice-wise DINOv2 framework; 150 slices per volume, global crops 96x96 and local crops 64x64 during SSL; images with severe artifacts, motion blur, or incomplete acquisition excluded
sources.split: per dataset 15% of volumes held out as a final test set never seen during pretraining, fine-tuning, or validation; remaining 85% used for five-fold stratified cross-validation (four folds ~70% train, one fold ~15% validation, best-validation checkpoint per fold, mean/SD across folds reported on the same held-out test set); pretraining/downstream dataset overlap acknowledged (mitigated only by the held-out test split)
sources.title: Towards Generalisable Foundation Models for Brain MRI
sources.uncertainty: mean and standard deviation across five cross-validation folds with two-sided t-tests on fold-level metrics, individual fold points shown on bar charts, and 95% confidence-interval bands in few-shot curves; no calibration, abstention, or conformal analysis

sources.code_weights: full 3DINO code public at https://github.com/AICONSlab/3DINO (pretraining, finetuning, visualization, inference); 3DINO-ViT weights stated to be made available upon paper acceptance
sources.cohort: pretraining on 98,815 unlabeled 3D volumes from 35 public/internal studies (MRI 70,434; CT 27,815; brain PET 566; >24-slice filter; deduplicated subsets of fastMRI knee, RSNA-ICH, NLST, 4D-Lung); downstream: BraTS 2021 1,084 patients (TCGA overlap removed; 758/108/218 train/val/test), BTCV 20/4/6, ICBM 756/151/233 scans (age bins 20–60), COVID-CT-MD 214/30/61, LA-SEG 80/20/54, TDSC-ABUS 70/10/20
sources.confound_audit: not_reported (PCA and multi-head self-attention visualizations of representations qualitatively inspected; no explicit scanner/site/cohort confound representation probe)
sources.design_impact: This preprint overlaps CAFT dimension d1 as a natively 3D, DINOv2-style generalist medical-imaging foundation model whose pretraining mix is 70,434 MRI volumes including brain MRI plus a small 566-volume brain-PET subset. Its quantified label-efficiency gains (BraTS Dice 0.90 with 10% labels vs 0.87 random-init at 100%, linear-decoder gains of 61% Dice on BTCV and 15% on BraTS, and ICBM brain-age AUC +5.3% average) make it a credible alternative global-embedding backbone for the BrainIAC-style encoder in d1. However, it evaluates no PET-defined diagnostic endpoints (so no d3 amyloid-status inference despite PET scans in pretraining), performs no cohort/scanner confound probing (d4), and offers no ambiguity-aware abstention or conformal prediction (d5).
sources.endpoint: 3DINO (DINOv2 adapted to native 3D: image-level self-distillation + iBOT-style patch objective, ViT-Large, 3D ViT-Adapter for dense tasks) evaluated on BraTS 2021 and BTCV segmentation (Dice/HD95), ICBM brain-age-binned classification and COVID-CT-MD lung classification (AUC/F1), and out-of-distribution LA-SEG (unseen organ) and TDSC-ABUS (unseen modality) segmentation, across 5–100% labeled-data fractions plus frozen linear-decoder segmentation probes
sources.external_validation: yes in the out-of-distribution sense — left atrium MRI (unseen organ) and 3D breast ultrasound (completely unseen modality) significantly outperform SOTA baselines (e.g., +24% Dice on TDSC-ABUS and +1.9% on LA-SEG at 25% labels); no site/scanner-stratified cohort validation
sources.modality: multi-organ multi-modality 3D medical imaging, predominantly MRI and CT with a small brain-PET subset; downstream tasks span brain MRI (BraTS, ICBM T1w), abdominal CT, cardiac MRI, and 3D breast ultrasound
sources.preprocessing: no atlas registration for pretraining, finetuning, or visualization; intensity normalization by linearly mapping 0.05th–99.95th percentiles to [-1, 1]; single-channel pretraining with channel-wise pass-through plus linear channel mixing for multi-channel downstream inputs; ICBM skull-stripped via iCVMapp3r; BraTS scans already skull-stripped and coregistered; 16^3 patches, 96^3 (then 112^3 high-resolution adaptation) inputs
sources.split: random per-dataset train/validation/test splits (counts above); BraTS finetuning set explicitly purged of TCGA-GBM/LGG scans present in the pretraining corpus to avoid evaluation bias; frozen encoder with tuned 3D ViT-Adapter + convolutional decoder for segmentation, linear probing (grid-searched layers/tokens) for classification; identical labeled-data subsets shared across compared methods
sources.title: A generalizable 3D framework and model for self-supervised learning in medical imaging
sources.uncertainty: 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals from 1,000 resamples of item-wise Dice/HD95 (segmentation) and from five randomized runs (classification); paired nonparametric Wilcoxon tests for segmentation and Welch's t-tests for classification; no calibration, abstention, or conformal analysis
